2.text: during the three years of his stay at Anadyr, kept a detailed account of all

3.text: sales and purchases, debits and credits, of the Russianized natives.¹
3.note: mz text read the footnote-1 body marker as ']'; raster shows superscript ¹ U+00B9 SUPERSCRIPT ONE, per §2.10.

4.text: I know another official who at the very same time held sway on the

5.text: Lower Kolyma, and who, in order to exterminate syphilis, kept another account,

6.text: not less detailed, of all sexual intercourse between men and women, hoping

7.text: in this way to find the bearers of the original disease. Both records were

8.text: failures, but they are very characteristic for the whole system of the adminis-

10.text: TRADE IN ALCOHOL. — I made mention before of the brisk trade in

11.text: strong liquor which is carried on in the Kolyma country between the Russians

12.text: and the Chukchee.² A few more words regarding this matter may be inter-
12.note: mz text had ASCII '2'; raster shows superscript ² U+00B2 SUPERSCRIPT TWO (footnote-2 body marker), per §2.10.

13.text: esting. In the thirties of the nineteenth century, liquor was still very scarce at

14.text: the Anui fair. Only the aged interpreter Kobelev, whose name has already

15.text: been mentioned, was able to sell some at retail. The price of the liquor was

16.text: a marten-skin for a small glassful. One of the documents adds, that because

17.text: of this traffic, he was greatly loved by all the people. At the same time,

18.text: however (1827), Nishne-Kolymsk had a regular saloon, where even fruit-brandy

19.text: (five barrels³) was sold. In 1842 there was a great famine on the Lower
19.note: mz text had ASCII '8'; raster clearly shows superscript ³ U+00B3 SUPERSCRIPT THREE (footnote-3 body marker), per §2.10.

20.text: Kolyma, and some cases of death by starvation on both Anui Rivers. In

21.text: the same year the saloon above mentioned sold thirty barrels of undiluted

22.text: alcohol, and in 1847 even fifty barrels. In 1864 the price of alcohol at the

23.text: Anui fair was two beaver-skins for one bottle.

24.text: From that time on, the imports of alcohol into the Kolyma country

25.text: increased quite regularly until they reached three hundred barrels yearly. At

26.text: the same time the price regularly decreased. During my stay on the Kolyma,

27.text: the price of alcohol in the saloons of Sredne-Kolymsk was two or two and a

28.text: half rubles per bottle. The saloon of Nishne-Kolymsk was abolished, but

29.text: plenty of liquor was to be had on the Lower Kolyma. The price at the

30.text: Anui fair was a red fox-skin per bottle, which is five times cheaper than the

31.text: price in 1864. In 1895 the Cossack commander of Sredne-Kolymsk, by

32.text: official order, sent a man to the Reindeer Chukchee of the western tundra

33.text: to buy reindeer for alcohol, only in the order the alcohol was called simply

34.text: “liquor.” The man brought with him one barrel of this liquor, and slaughtered
34.note: mz text used straight quotes; keyed curly “…” per §1, R1.

35.text: twenty-two reindeer. I was a witness to the whole transaction. I was informed
35.note: mz text carried a trailing comma not present in print; the line ends on the bare word 'informed', per R9.

36.text: ¹ After the energetic activity of Mr. Gondatti, there came for the Anadyr a period of quiet. So the

38.text: two thousand rubles for the investigation of the country, and to Gondatti fifteen hundred rubles. Now we

39.text: consider that the country is thoroughly investigated. And you are to be, not an investigator, but a simple

40.text: chief of the district.” I may agree with the idea expressed in these words, in so far as the less active the
40.note: mz text used a straight closing quote; keyed curly ” per §1, R1 — closes the quotation opened on L37 ('You must remember...').

41.text: representative of the Russian authority is, the better it is for the inhabitants of the country.
